events.title: Rebel barons renounce their allegiance to King John
events.description: A group of English barons formally withdrew their fealty from John and took up arms. Their capture of London weeks later forced the king to agree to Magna Carta in June.
events.html: A group of English barons formally withdrew their fealty from John and took up arms. Their capture of London weeks later forced the king to agree to Magna Carta in June.

events.title: Kublai Khan becomes Great Khan of the Mongol Empire
events.description: Kublai Khan, a grandson of Genghis Khan, was crowned Great Khan of the Mongol Empire. His disputed succession contributed to the empire's fragmentation; in 1271 he proclaimed the Yuan dynasty in China, which he ruled until 1294.
events.html: Kublai Khan, a grandson of Genghis Khan, was crowned Great Khan of the Mongol Empire. His disputed succession contributed to the empire's fragmentation; in 1271 he proclaimed the Yuan dynasty in China, which he ruled until 1294.

events.title: Estates-General opens at Versailles
events.description: Louis XVI convened the Estates-General for the first time since 1614 to resolve a financial crisis. Disputes over voting led the Third Estate to declare itself the National Assembly in June.
events.html: Louis XVI convened the Estates-General for the first time since 1614 to resolve a financial crisis. Disputes over voting led the Third Estate to declare itself the National Assembly in June.

events.title: Napoleon dies in exile on St Helena
events.description: Napoleon Bonaparte died aged 51 on the remote Atlantic island where the British had held him since 1815. His legal code and the states he redrew outlived his empire.
events.html: Napoleon Bonaparte died aged 51 on the remote Atlantic island where the British had held him since 1815. His legal code and the states he redrew outlived his empire.

events.title: Continental Europe's first passenger railway opens in Belgium
events.description: Trains began running between Brussels and Mechelen on the first state-built passenger line on the European mainland. Newly independent Belgium soon had a national rail network.
events.html: Trains began running between Brussels and Mechelen on the first state-built passenger line on the European mainland. Newly independent Belgium soon had a national rail network.

events.title: Mexican army defeats the French at Puebla
events.description: General Ignacio Zaragoza's outnumbered troops repulsed a French assault on Puebla. The victory, marked as Cinco de Mayo, delayed but did not prevent the French occupation of Mexico.
events.html: General Ignacio Zaragoza's outnumbered troops repulsed a French assault on Puebla. The victory, marked as Cinco de Mayo, delayed but did not prevent the French occupation of Mexico.

events.title: Tchaikovsky helps open New York's Music Hall, later Carnegie Hall
events.description: Andrew Carnegie's new concert hall opened with a festival at which Tchaikovsky conducted. Renamed Carnegie Hall in 1893, it became America's most famous concert venue.
events.html: Andrew Carnegie's new concert hall opened with a festival at which Tchaikovsky conducted. Renamed Carnegie Hall in 1893, it became America's most famous concert venue.

events.title: Alan Shepard becomes the first American in space
events.description: Alan Shepard made a 15-minute suborbital flight in Freedom 7, three weeks after Gagarin's orbit. Twenty days later President Kennedy committed the US to landing a man on the Moon.
events.html: Alan Shepard made a 15-minute suborbital flight in Freedom 7, three weeks after Gagarin's orbit. Twenty days later President Kennedy committed the US to landing a man on the Moon.
